name: bluebird-promisify-multiargs-balena-request
behavioral_change: In bluebird v_new (3.0.0), `Promise.promisify` and `Promise.promisifyAll` by default resolve the promise with only the first success value passed to the node-style callback, whereas v_old (2.x) collected multiple success values into an array. The call form is unchanged and no exception is raised by the library itself; the old array behaviour is restored with the new `multiArgs: true` option.
downstream_effect: balena-request's lib/request.coffee promisifies the `request` module, whose callback yields `(err, response, body)`, and consumes the result with `.spread (response) ->`; after the upgrade the promise resolves to the bare response object and `.spread` throws `TypeError: expecting an array or an iterable object`, so 22 tests fail with rejected promises and mismatched assertions. The output never names lib/request.coffee, promisify or spread; stack frames point at the test file and node_modules only, and the many bluebird paths identify the library but not the mechanism.
reference_fix: The reference fix changes one line in lib/request.coffee, adding `multiArgs: true` to the `Promise.promisify` call on line 23.
documented_in: bluebird's "New in bluebird 3.0" document (docs/docs/new-in-bluebird-3.md, tag v3.7.2), section Promisification API changes, states in prose that promisification now uses only the first callback argument and that a new boolean option `multiArgs` restores the array behaviour. The document gives only prose for this change and no code showing `Promise.promisify(fn, {multiArgs: true})`.
failing_tests: 22 failing tests, listed in pinned/STATE-NEW.log; for example: Request: given the token is always fresh .send() given a simple GET endpoint given an absolute url should allow passing a baseUrl
